SECTION 01

Classifications & Benefits

The employee categories and benefits listed in the PDF

01

Employee Classifications

PDF p. 2
  • According to rank: managerial, supervisory, and rank-and-file.
  • According to nature of engagement: regular, non-regular, and casual.

Statutory Benefits — Work and Pay

PDF p. 3
  • Overtime pay; night shift differential; premium pay; holiday pay; service charges; normal hours of work; weekly rest period.

Statutory Benefits — Leave

PDF p. 3
  • Service incentive leave; parental leave; maternity leave; paternity leave; special leave for women employees; leave for victims of violence against women and children (VAWC).
SECTION 02

Service Incentive Leave (SIL)

Five leave credits, yearly renewal, and listed exemptions

02

Service Incentive Leave

PDF p. 4
  • Paid leave credits used during absence from work.
  • The slide describes five (5) SIL credits after at least 12 months of service and lists “managerial/rank-and-file” in this explanation.
  • The employer must pay the cash equivalent of unused SIL credits.
  • SIL credits replenish yearly.

Exemptions Listed on the Following Slide

PDF p. 5
  • Government employees; persons in the personal service of another.
  • Managerial employees and officers or members of a managerial staff; field personnel.
  • Employees already enjoying the benefit or at least five days of paid vacation leave.
  • Employees of establishments regularly employing fewer than ten (10) persons.

SIL Illustration — 14 Months

PDF p. 6
  • The slide’s example gives Mr. X five SIL credits for his first-year anniversary and one additional SIL credit for two months of his second year.
  • Example’s stated total: six (6) SIL credits for 14 months of service.
SECTION 03

Solo Parent Leave

RA 8972 as presented in the source

03

Solo Parent Leave — Benefit

PDF p. 7
  • Seven (7) working days of full-pay leave for covered solo parents to perform parental duties.
  • Leave pay equals basic salary plus mandatory and/or integrated allowances and must not be lower than minimum wage.

Solo Parent Leave — Requirements

PDF p. 8
  • At least one year of service, continuous or broken.
  • Notify the employer within a reasonable period.
  • Present a Solo Parent Identification Card, which the slide says may be obtained from the DSWD office in the city or municipality of residence.

Solo Parent Leave — Additional Conditions

PDF p. 9
  • Apply in reasonable time so the employer can adjust for the absence.
  • The benefit is not convertible to cash.
  • Solo parent employees may request a flexible work schedule as long as productivity and the employer-defined core work hours are not adversely affected.
SECTION 04

Maternity Leave

Duration, rules, and conditions stated in the PDF

04

Maternity Leave — Duration

PDF p. 10
  • One hundred five (105) days of leave with full pay.
  • May extend for thirty (30) additional days without pay.
  • Female solo parents receive an additional fifteen (15) days with full pay.

Maternity Leave — Coverage and Rules

PDF p. 11
  • Extended to pregnant female employees, whether single or married, for pregnancy, miscarriage, or emergency termination of pregnancy, regardless of frequency.
  • Not convertible to cash and not cumulative.
  • The employer advances full payment within thirty (30) days of filing the maternity leave application.

Maternity Leave — Conditions

PDF p. 12
  • SSS member who paid at least three (3) monthly contributions in the 12-month period immediately preceding the semester of childbirth, miscarriage, or emergency termination of pregnancy.
  • Must notify the employer about pregnancy and probable childbirth date for transmission to the SSS.
SECTION 05

Paternity Leave

Covered male employees and their entitlement

05

Paternity Leave — Benefit

PDF p. 13
  • Seven (7) days with full pay for married male employees whose lawful wife gives birth or experiences miscarriage.
  • Applies regardless of employment status.
  • The slide states the benefit applies to the first four (4) deliveries of the lawful wife with whom the employee cohabits.

Paternity Leave — Application and Cash

PDF p. 15
  • Apply within reasonable time of the expected delivery, or according to company rules or a collective bargaining agreement.
  • For a miscarriage, prior application is not required.
  • Living separately because of workstation or occupation does not remove the benefit according to this slide.
  • Not convertible to cash if not availed.

Paternity Leave — Conditions

PDF p. 16
  • Employee at the time of the child’s delivery.
  • Cohabiting with the spouse at childbirth or miscarriage.
  • Properly applied for paternity leave, under the stated timing requirements.
  • Lawful wife has given birth or suffered a miscarriage.
SECTION 06

Leave for VAWC

RA 9262 as described in the module

06

VAWC Leave — Purpose & Documentation

PDF p. 17
  • Republic Act 9262 is described as the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004.
  • Leave covers days needed for medical and legal matters.
  • Present certification of a pending action from the punong barangay, barangay kagawad, prosecutor, or clerk of court as applicable.

VAWC Leave — Duration

PDF p. 18
  • Up to ten (10) days of leave with full pay.
  • Full pay comprises basic salary and mandatory allowances fixed by the Regional Wage Board.
  • Not convertible to cash and not cumulative.
SECTION 07

Special Leave for Women

RA 9710 — surgery due to gynecological disorders

07

Special Leave for Women — Benefit

PDF p. 19
  • Female employees regardless of age and civil status.
  • Two (2) months with full pay based on gross monthly compensation: monthly basic pay plus mandatory allowances fixed by regional wage boards.
  • Granted after qualifying surgery; the employer may allow pay before or during surgery.

Special Leave — Cash and Accumulation

PDF p. 20
  • Non-cumulative and non-convertible to cash unless the collective bargaining agreement provides otherwise.

Special Leave — Conditions

PDF p. 21
  • At least six (6) months of continuous aggregate employment service in the twelve (12) months before surgery.
  • Apply within reasonable time of the expected surgery or according to employer rules or collective bargaining agreement.
  • Must have undergone surgery for gynecological disorders certified by a competent physician.
SECTION 08

Premium Pay & Overtime

Definitions and rates illustrated in the module

08

Premium Pay

PDF p. 22
  • Additional compensation for work performed within eight (8) hours on rest days and special days.
  • Slides 23–24 provide computed cases; see the original slide illustrations below.

Overtime Pay

PDF p. 25
  • Additional compensation for work beyond eight (8) hours a day.
  • The PDF states that its coverage is the same as previously discussed for SIL.

Rates and Calculation Illustrations

PDF p. 26–30
  • The PDF presents tables of overtime pay rates for ordinary working days, rest days, special days, and combinations with holidays.
  • The original slides supply peso amounts, rates, and worked calculation steps; use the enlarged slide references below to read the original tables and examples.

Overtime Activity Instructions

PDF p. 31–40
  • Compute the total day’s pay, including regular and overtime compensation if applicable.
  • Show the complete solution step by step.
  • Round to the nearest centavo (₱0.01).
  • Original slide examples and activities are retained as images below, without invented answer keys.
SECTION 09

Leave Compliance Audit

The PDF’s three practice cases (not answered)

09

Activity 1 — Leave Compliance Audit

PDF p. 41
  • HR Strategy & Compliance activity, in small groups of 3–4 students.
  • Groups act as an HR Compliance Committee to determine leave entitlements, supporting documentation, and statutory pay rules.

Case 1 — Elena

PDF p. 42
  • Senior female specialist with two years of service, requiring 45 days away after surgery for a uterine fibroid.
  • A single mother with Solo Parent ID who already used three SIL days this year.

Case 2 — Carla

PDF p. 43
  • Regular full-time graphic designer with three years of service, injured in a domestic violence incident and needing emergency surgery.
  • Granted 10-day VAWC leave (RA 9262), holds Solo Parent ID (RA 8972 / RA 11861), and has five unused SIL days.

Case 3 — Mark

PDF p. 44
  • Senior plant technician with four years of service applying for paternity leave (RA 8187) after birth of first child by C-section.
  • His paternity leave overlaps a two-day regular holiday, and he later works an emergency ten-hour shift on a rest day during the same pay period.
